findings.title: Recovery codes written to user storage in plaintext
findings.description: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes `generatedCodes`, which are the raw codes from `RecoveryAuthnCodesBean.generateRawCodes()`, and passes that JSON to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The local path hashes the same codes first: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` runs each one through `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode` (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-67`). The user-storage path skips that step, so external storage such as an LDAP attribute or a customer database ends up holding usable second-factor secrets. The fixture is built around the raw values: it stores them (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:197`), compares raw input (`:340`), and re-hashes them in `getCredentials` (`:237`). Fix: persist only the hashed values, for example from the secret data `createFromValues` already builds. Then compare `hashRawCode(input)` in the provider, and build the model from the stored hashes without hashing them again.

findings.title: Old local recovery codes stay valid after regeneration when user storage accepts the write
findings.description: When `updateCredential` returns true, the method never removes an existing local `recovery-authn-codes` credential. The local path does remove it: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential` deletes the existing credential first (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-40`). At login, `UserCredentialManager.isValid(List)` tries the user-storage validator first. If that rejects the code, the input is still unmatched, so it falls through to every `CredentialInputValidator`, including `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid` (`UserCredentialManager.java:59-79`, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-112`). That provider matches the old local hash and accepts it, so a user who regenerated their codes can still log in with the revoked set. The authenticator's exhaustion check also reads the federated store first (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-61`), so depletion of the stale local set never triggers re-setup. This applies to a federated user who already had local codes, for example from before federation. Fix: in the user-storage branch, remove existing local credentials of this type.

findings.title: Codes validated by user storage are never consumed
findings.description: The fixture's `isValid` returns an `anyMatch` and never removes the used code. Core does not compensate. `UserCredentialManager.isValid` stops once the user-storage validator matches, so the local `removeRecoveryAuthnCode()` path never runs for federated codes (`UserCredentialManager.java:59-79`). `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (lines 78-92) never writes the federated credential back, so `allCodesUsed()` stays false and the regenerate prompt never appears. The result is that any stored code validates on every login. This is reachable only through a user-storage provider that opts in via `CredentialInputUpdater.supportsCredentialType`, but the change defines no consumption contract for those providers. The contract needs to be stated and enforced, with a test.

findings.title: Authenticator removes the exhausted credential from the wrong store
findings.description: After this change, `optUserCredentialFound` can be a federated `CredentialModel`. Lines 85-88 then call `removeStoredCredentialById(...getId())`, which deletes from the local store using a federated ID. That is a no-op at best and could hit an unrelated local row at worst. Because the lookup prefers federated, a depleted local set is also ignored whenever a federated set exists (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-61`). Restrict removal to local credentials, and check exhaustion on whichever set `isValid` actually consumed.

findings.title: Tests cover only the happy path of user-storage recovery codes
findings.description: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` checks a single login with code index 0. Nothing covers rejection of a wrong code, reuse of a code that has already logged in (this would expose the replay gap), regeneration (this would expose the stale-code defect), or exhaustion re-triggering setup. The user-storage branch in `CredentialHelper` and the new `getCredential` lookup are both untested on these paths. Add tests for these cases with the fixes.

findings.title: Circular dependency between two server-spi classes
findings.description: The new `getCredential` makes `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils` import `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, while that model already imports `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils` (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:13`). The cycle compiles, but it ties the two classes together. Moving `getCredential` onto the model would remove the cycle.

findings.title: Fixture swallows deserialization errors without the exception
findings.description: `getCredentials` catches `IOException` and logs a message without the exception, so the codes silently disappear from credential listings. Pass `e` to the logger.

findings.title: Naming and typo drift in the new code and tests
findings.description: Several small inconsistencies: the alias `"delayed-suthenticator-config"` (`:135`); a fully qualified `org.junit.Assert` at `:481` next to `org.keycloak.testsuite.Assert` used throughout the same file; the Javadoc typo "a optional  credential model" (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:54`); and the double space in the fixture's log message.

findings.title: Unrelated reformatting and a hardcoded provider ID
findings.description: The diff re-indents `getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory` from 4 to 8 spaces and reformats unrelated lines in the test and the fixture class Javadoc. These changes hide the real change, so they belong in a separate commit. Separately, `CredentialHelper.java:116` hardcodes `"keycloak-recovery-authn-codes"`, where the action used `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID`. The hardcode is probably necessary because `server-spi-private` cannot reference the `services` module, so a comment would help. The new method also lacks `@param`/`@return` Javadoc, unlike `createOTPCredential` directly above it (`CredentialHelper.java:87-91`).
